# dsh-interject
**English** | 中文

Delivers a queued chat message at the **next step boundary** instead of waiting for the whole
turn t
o finish — without aborting the model call that is already running.
A DeepSeek Harness **host plugin**. No client half, no WebUI changes, no `app.asar` edits.
## The problem

While an agent is working through a long turn (a single reasoning step can take minutes), a
message

you send mid-turn goes into the `next-turn` inbox queue. The loop only claims that queue
**after the
entire turn ends** — which may be many steps later.
## What this plugin does
DSH's inbox has two queues:
| Queue | Written by | Claimed at |

| `next-turn` | Enter while busy (queue and send) | **after the whole turn ends** |
| `next-step` |
Cmd/Ctrl+Enter (interject and send) | **the next step boundary** (one step = one model call plus its
Enter (interject and send) | **the next step boundary** (one step = one model call plus its tools) |

The plugin listens for `agent/inbox/inserted`. When the policy matches, it moves the message from
`n

ext-turn` into `next-step`. At the start of the next step the model sees your message in its
history
, and the reasoning currently in flight is not discarded at all.

**Why it cannot be read mid-generation:** `llm.stream(request)` freezes the `messages` array when
th

e request is built and the HTTP body is already on the wire — there is no channel to append
input du

ring generation. So there are only two options: wait for the call to finish (the default
here), or a
bort and resend (`interrupt`).
## Install
### From the plugin market

Search for `dsh-interject` in the DSH plugin market and install it. The market resolves the
package
from this repository.

`lib/index.js` — D
SH loads plugins as static ESM, so file edits do not affect a running process.
### Manual mounting (without the market)

`name` must be the **package name**, not an absolute path — the market matches loader entries by
nam
e, and an absolute path leaves the plugin card reading "installed, not loaded".
## Configuration
`~/.dsh/dsh-interject.json` — **hot-reloaded**, save the file and it takes effect; no restart.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Values | Meaning |
| `onQueue` | `steer` / `interrupt` / `pass` | What to do with a message that entered `next-turn`. `

steer` = promote it to `next-step` (**default, zero waste**) |
| `onSteer` | `pass` / `interrupt` |
What to do with a message that entered `next-step`. `pass` = hands off (**default**, it already wait

s for the next boundary) |
| `interruptWhile` | `thinking` / `always` | When a hard interrupt is all
owed; with `thinking`, the tool-running phase degrades to a soft interjection instead of killing a l

ong command |
| `graceMs` | ms | Delay after a hit, so messages sent in one batch are merged |
| `co

oldownMs` | ms | Minimum gap between two hard interrupts on one agent |
| `includeSubagents` | bool

| Also handle sub-agents (default: only root sessions you can see) |
| `stallMs` | ms, `0` disables

| Write a "still running" line to the log when a single step exceeds this |
| `wakeFallbackMs` | ms,
`0` disables | How long to wait for the driver to report idle after a hard interrupt; only used on

the degraded path |
| `bootMarker` | bool | Write `~/.dsh/dsh-interject-boot.json` (version / pid /

effective config) |
| `log` | bool | Diagnostic log switch |

**The default never interrupts.** To make Cmd/Ctrl+Enter a preemption gesture:
`{"onSteer": "interru
pt"}`. To switch the plugin off: `{"enabled": false}`.

Environment overrides: `DSH_INTERJECT_CONFIG` (config path), `DSH_INTERJECT_LOG` (log path;
empty st
ring disables logging), `DSH_INTERJECT_BOOT` (boot marker path).
## Does it cost more tokens?
**Not with the default configuration.** The plugin sends no extra requests; it only moves a pending

message to a different queue. The only increment is that the message enters history earlier, so
the
remaining requests in this turn carry it once more — a prompt-cache prefix hit, which is cheap.

Only `interrupt` really costs: the aborted request's produced output is billed as usual, and then
a
full history is resent.

## Compatibility

Declared: `>=0.2.0-rc.1` with no upper bound. The source of three host versions was read line by
lin
e to confirm the public surface this plugin uses:
| Version | Status |

| `0.2.0-rc.2` | verified (development host) |
| `0.2.1-rc.5` | verified (npm `latest` / `next`) |
|
`0.2.2-alpha.2` | verified (npm `alpha`) |

Every capability is **probed, not assumed** — the plugin imports no `@deepseek-ai/*` package and
use

s only the `ctx` / `agent` objects the host passes in. That is not for the sake of older
versions: i

t is so a future rename of an internal field degrades the plugin instead of breaking it.
Anything un

detectable falls back to a public path (for example, no `phase` means "wait for
`agent/status` to re
port idle, then `steer`" instead of the wake latch).

The three versions agree on: `ctx.agents.get/roots`, `agent.session`, `agent.status`,
`agent.inbox.{

nextTurn,nextStep,hasPending,claim,append,prepend,replace,remove,splice}`,
`agent.followup/steer/inj

ect/cancel`, the session events `step/start`, `step/end`, `turn/end`,
`assistant/message`, `assistan

t/attempt`, `tool/call`, `tool/result`, `agent/inbox/inserted`
(payload `{agent, message}`), `agent/

disposed` (payload `{agent}`), `message.source.kind === 'user'`,
and the internal field `agent.phase

ad `{agent}`), `message.source.kind === 'user'`,
and the internal field `agent.phase.wakeRequested`.
